decisive_items: alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition
new patchy peribronchovascular consolidations in the right upper lobe, left upper lobe, and left lower-lobe apical segment
Repeat BAL was negative for AFB, fungus, and Pneumocystis jirovecii
response.rationale: The biopsy shows an organizing pneumonia pattern, and the new consolidations appear after treated PJP with a negative repeat BAL, making post-infectious organizing pneumonia the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.why: IgA nephropathy is the underlying renal disease, not the cause of the pulmonary infiltrates.
Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome is a chronic lung-transplant airway complication; there is no airflow obstruction or bronchiolar obliteration.
Tacrolimus-induced pneumonitis is not supported by the biopsy and lacks a clear drug relationship.
Mycophenolate pulmonary toxicity is not supported by the biopsy; the clinical course favors organizing pneumonia.
Idiopathic pneumonia syndrome is an HSCT-related diffuse lung injury, not a renal-transplant complication; the biopsy shows organizing pneumonia.
PJP was the initial infection and resolved; repeat BAL is negative, so it does not explain the current organizing pneumonia.
